Let’s step into Chapter 1: Growing Up in a World of Privilege and Uncertainty.
Imagine a life where comfort and caution walk hand in hand. That’s how it was for one Moroccan family, living in a world shaped by both privilege and the shadows of uncertainty.
The eldest daughter grew up in the glow of royal palaces—a place where luxury was the norm, and political whispers filled the air. Her father, always moving with purpose and a touch of wariness, stood close to the king. He was a powerful man, but he never forgot that power can be as fleeting as it is intoxicating.
Day-to-day life? It was filled with all the markers of the elite: grand meals, lessons in perfect manners, and the quiet, ever-watchful presence of servants who seemed to know everything and nothing, all at once.
Still, you could feel it—that gentle tension beneath the surface. The comfort they enjoyed always felt a bit fragile, as if it could slip away at any moment. The children, especially the eldest, picked up on the smallest signals. Laughter that didn’t quite ring true. Conversations that ended with just a glance. Even the palace itself, for all its beauty, held secrets in every corner.
The king was both a generous protector and a distant, almost unpredictable figure. At any moment, he could call for the family—or turn away. Their mother, graceful and fiercely strong, tried her best to shield her children from the waves of fear that sometimes swept through their halls.
And in the midst of it all, the eldest daughter found herself both included and apart. She played with royal children, joined in their lessons and games, but deep down, she always knew she was different. Her family’s loyalty was expected—yet never quite trusted. The rules weren’t written down, but everyone understood them: loyalty meant everything, and even the faintest hint of betrayal could bring disaster.
Over time, the rhythms of palace life became second nature. The children learned when to speak, when to smile, and when to keep their thoughts tucked safely away. Their father’s status brought both admiration and suspicion. The family’s fortunes rose and fell with the tides of politics, so they adapted, finding small joys and comfort in each other—knowing that everything could change without warning.
Looking back, those early lessons—learning to read a room, to hide fear, to find strength in each other—became their lifeline. Because soon, the world they knew would disappear overnight. But the resilience they built in those palace halls? That’s what would help them survive what came next.
